params.question: A community physician investigates whether weekly iron-folic acid supplementation reduces anaemia prevalence among pregnant women attending a rural PHC, compared to standard antenatal care. In this PICO-structured question, what does 'standard antenatal care' represent?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Population refers to the group being studied — here, pregnant women at the rural PHC. 'Standard antenatal care' is the reference against which the intervention is evaluated, not the study group itself.

Correct! In PICO, Comparison (C) is the alternative against which the intervention is judged. Without a clearly defined comparator, the study cannot determine whether the intervention offers any added benefit.

The Intervention is the exposure being tested — here, weekly iron-folic acid supplementation. 'Standard antenatal care' is the existing practice it is being compared against, not the experimental exposure.
The Outcome is what the study measures — here, anaemia prevalence. 'Standard antenatal care' defines the comparator group, not the study endpoint.

overallFeedback.feedback: In PICO, the Comparison (C) is the existing practice or placebo against which the Intervention is evaluated. Here, 'standard antenatal care' is the comparator for iron-folic acid supplementation.
Well done! Identifying the Comparison component ensures the research question includes a reference group — essential for drawing valid conclusions from any study.

interactions.label: A health worker records the birth weights (in grams) of 9 neonates at a PHC: 210

params.question: A health worker records the birth weights (in grams) of 9 neonates at a PHC: 2100, 2400, 2500, 2600, 2700, 2800, 2900, 3000, and 4800. Which measure of central tendency best represents the typical birth weight in this group?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The arithmetic mean would be inflated by the extreme outlier (4,800 g), yielding a value higher than 8 of the 9 observations. For skewed data with outliers, the mean misrepresents the typical value.
Standard deviation is a measure of dispersion (spread), not central tendency. It tells you how far values deviate from the mean but does not indicate the typical value.

Correct! The median (2,700 g) is the middle value when data are arranged in ascending order, and is unaffected by the extreme outlier. When data contain outliers or are skewed, the median better represents the central position.
The mode is the most frequently occurring value. In this dataset no value repeats, so the mode is undefined. Even when defined, the mode rarely represents the centre of a continuous distribution.

overallFeedback.feedback: When data are skewed by extreme values, the median is preferred over the mean because it is not pulled towards outliers. Here, the median (2,700 g) better represents typical birth weight than the outlier-inflated mean.
Exactly right. In clinical data with outliers — such as an unusually heavy neonate — the median provides a more reliable summary of typical values than the mean.

interactions.label: A researcher compares mean haemoglobin levels among women in three independent g

params.question: A researcher compares mean haemoglobin levels among women in three independent groups — urban, semi-urban, and rural. The data are approximately normally distributed with equal variances. Which statistical test is most appropriate?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! Applying the four factors: (1) outcome is continuous (Hb level), (2) three groups to compare, (3) groups are independent, and (4) data are normally distributed — all parametric assumptions are satisfied, pointing to one-way ANOVA.
The paired t-test compares two related measurements in the same subjects (e.g. before and after). Here there are three independent groups, so a paired t-test is inapplicable on both counts.
The chi-square test is used for categorical outcome variables (e.g. proportions). Haemoglobin is a continuous variable, so a chi-square test is inappropriate regardless of the number of groups.

The Kruskal-Wallis test is the non-parametric alternative to one-way ANOVA, used when data do NOT meet normality assumptions. Since the data here are normally distributed, the parametric ANOVA is preferred.

overallFeedback.feedback: Apply the four factors in sequence: (1) continuous outcome → not chi-square; (2) three groups → not a two-sample test; (3) independent groups → not paired; (4) normal distribution → parametric ANOVA, not Kruskal-Wallis.
Well done! Systematically applying the four decision factors — variable type, number of groups, independence, and distribution — leads directly to the correct test.

interactions.label: The Block Medical Officer computes the following summary for BMI-for-age z-score

params.question: The Block Medical Officer computes the following summary for BMI-for-age z-scores of 400 sampled adolescent girls: mean = −1.8, median = −1.2, SD = 1.5. What does the substantial difference between the mean and median indicate about this dataset?

answers.text: The sample size is too small to draw conclusions

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A sample of 400 is more than adequate. The mean–median discrepancy reflects the shape of the distribution, not the sample size.
In a normal distribution the mean and median are approximately equal. A large gap between them indicates the data are NOT symmetric.

answers.text: The standard deviation has been calculated incorrectly

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The standard deviation measures spread and is independent of the mean–median relationship. A large SD indicates wide variability but does not explain why the mean and median differ.

answers.text: The distribution is negatively skewed, with a few extremely low values pulling the mean down

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! When the mean is substantially lower than the median, the distribution has a left (negative) tail. A subgroup of severely undernourished girls is dragging the mean below the median — a clinically important finding that warrants targeted intervention.

overallFeedback.feedback: When the mean is pulled below the median, the distribution is negatively skewed — a few extremely low values (severely undernourished girls) drag the mean down. Recognising this pattern is a key skill in interpreting descriptive statistics.

Excellent! Comparing the mean and median is a quick check for skewness. When they diverge, the distribution is non-symmetric — clinically, this often reveals a vulnerable subgroup that needs targeted attention.
